claims.text: Increasing Cr concentration in CoCrFeMnNi will produce a more robust, adherent, and self-healing passive oxide film.
Adding a small amount of Mo to CoCrFeMnNi will produce a denser and more self-healing passive oxide film.
The protective passive layer formed on the modified alloy will be rich in Cr oxides.
Greater passive-film adherence and integrity will improve resistance to mechanical removal during simultaneous wear and corrosion.
The improved passive film will rapidly repassivate freshly exposed metal during cyclic wear.
The improved passive film will act as a barrier against corrosion.
The improved passive film will prevent or reduce electrolyte ingress into mechanically abraded areas.
Rapid repassivation and reduced electrolyte ingress will minimize synergistic damage from concurrent wear and corrosion.
Under combined wear and corrosion, the Cr-enriched or Mo-containing alloy will have lower wear volume than the baseline CoCrFeMnNi alloy.
Under combined wear and corrosion, the Cr-enriched or Mo-containing alloy will have lower corrosion current density than the baseline alloy.
The modified and baseline alloys will show little difference in isolated wear tests.
The modified and baseline alloys will show little difference in isolated corrosion tests.
The predicted improvement should hold under controlled cyclic sliding in a moderate corrosive environment such as 3.5% NaCl at room temperature.
Excessively severe wear may diminish or eliminate the benefit of the modified passive film.
A substantially more aggressive corrosive environment may diminish or eliminate the predicted benefit.
Compositional modification may compromise mechanical toughness and thereby reduce the expected improvement.
A comparison of compositionally modified and baseline samples under matched combined, wear-only, and corrosion-only conditions can test the proposed synergy mechanism.

Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in both wear volume and corrosion current density under combined conditions, while isolated behavior remains similar, would falsify the hypothesis.
